purpose_text: DETAIL. Develops streamline and body position by adding a glide while one arm remains extended toward the wall.
how: Take 3 strokes, and then glide with one arm extended forward and the other at the side while remaining completely still and as streamlined as possible. Use pull buoys for additional effect. Do not kick.

name_en: FREE WILLY aka. FREESTYLE WITH DOLPHIN KICK
purpose_text: DETAIL. Increases arm speed in freestyle, develops the dolphin kick, and works the core.
how: Use freestyle arms with a dolphin kick. Time the downward kick with hand entry, using 1 kick per stroke. The rhythm requires practice.

name_en: FREE & LAZY aka. 2 BEAT KICK DRILL
purpose_text: APPRECIATION. Slows the drill so that the swimmer can focus on upper-body movement while pulling without a buoy.
how: Swim freestyle very slowly with only 1 leg kick per stroke.

name_en: TARZAN DRILL aka. WATER POLO FREE
purpose_text: APPRECIATION, DETAIL. Demonstrates the importance of a strong kick for stability, develops high elbows and a stable head position, and allows observation of hand entry.
how: Swim with the head above the water and the chin at water level, similar to the position associated with Johnny Weissmuller. Direct the eyes toward the opposite wall or the hands entering in front. Observing the hands helps the swimmer check whether they enter palm-down rather than thumb-first. The head may be lowered gradually toward the water while swimming to practice stable head position and hand entry. Keep the head still while the shoulders rotate, and avoid moving the head erratically.

warnings.reason: Keeping the head continuously above water during freestyle may increase strain on the neck, lower back, and shoulders. Restrict the drill to short, controlled repetitions.

purpose_text: DETAIL. Encourages a straighter and more complete flutter kick while reducing corkscrew movement of the legs and feet during breathing.
how: Kick with increased intensity while maintaining a slow, deliberate arm tempo. The kick tempo should be at least twice the arm tempo.

purpose_text: ESSENTIAL, DETAIL. Corrects breathing, body position, and head position while engaging the core to maintain a stable body line.
how: Place a paddle on the forehead and swim while directing it forward. Some swimmers may also perform turns with the paddle in place, although this is an advanced variation.

warnings.reason: Holding a paddle on the forehead while swimming or turning may restrict vision and create facial or wall-impact risk. Use only at low speed in a clear lane with direct supervision.

purpose_text: DETAIL. Reinforces cross-body coordination.
how: Swim with 1 fin on one leg and 1 paddle on the opposite hand.

purpose_text: DETAIL. Develops freestyle catch position, stroke extension, stroke length, and hip rotation.
how: Move the recovering arm to the catch position, reverse the recovery to return the hand to the hip, and then move the arm forward again beyond the original catch point while rotating fully onto the side. Keep the elbow high.

purpose_text: BEGINNER, DETAIL. Develops a high-elbow catch, establishes pressure on the water at the start of the catch, and supports body position.
how: Use a freestyle kick, or use only a pull buoy, while sculling with high elbows. Perform the movement without rushing and use a snorkel.

purpose_text: APPRECIATION, DETAIL. Develops arm shape and position and feel for the water throughout the pull cycle.
how: Use a freestyle kick or pull buoy. Begin sculling in front and gradually move the sculling position toward the hips by the end of the length.

purpose_text: BEGINNER, PROGRESSION. Develops breathing timing as a variation of holding the wall with 1 arm and breathing to the side.
how:
Step 1: At the wall, hold the wall with 1 arm extended and keep the other arm at the side. Kick and breathe toward the side of the lowered arm every 6 kicks.
Step 2: Keep 1 arm at the side and 1 arm extended, and swim lengths with fins if needed while breathing every 6 kicks.
Step 3: Swim full freestyle with or without fins to integrate the movement.

purpose_text: DETAIL, APPRECIATION. Develops front-quadrant timing and forward reach toward the wall.
how: Perform a long dog-paddle action with the head in the water and the arms extending fully backward and forward. During recovery, slide the arms underwater, fingers-first and close to the body. Do not begin the next arm action until the other arm has nearly reached the front.

purpose_text: DETAIL, BEGINNER. Develops balance and high-elbow recovery.
how: Hold the underwater arm straight in front of the shoulder without allowing it to drop, and rotate the hip until the swimmer is fully on the side. Hold the recovering arm with a high elbow and the hand relaxed near the goggles, like a puppet on strings. Kick for 8 to 10 kicks, and then transition quickly to the opposite side using the torso to drive the switch. Pause with the other hand relaxed near the goggles. Fins make the drill easier.

warnings.reason: Holding a side position for 8-10 kicks and then switching sharply may increase rotational stress at the shoulder and lower back. Control the speed and range of the transition.

purpose_text: BEGINNER. Develops distance per stroke.
how: While swimming, focus on reaching toward the wall with every stroke. This cue is easy for young swimmers to understand.

purpose_text: DETAIL, APPRECIATION. Develops kick efficiency, hip-driven rotation, side breathing without lifting the head, and core control.
how: Begin kicking on the stomach with the arms at the sides. Perform 6 kicks in the prone position, rotate from the hips to the side for 6 kicks, return to the front for 6 kicks, and then rotate to the other side for 6 kicks. Maintain a long neck with the eyes directed downward and initiate rotation from the hips rather than the shoulders. This position should make side breathing easier.

purpose_text: APPRECIATION. Focuses on slowing down, maintaining correct technique, and preserving body position.
how: After completing other freestyle drills or at the end of practice, integrate the skills and swim freestyle with correct technique as quietly as possible. Minimize splashing, attend to the feel and sound of the water, and remain relaxed.

purpose_text: DETAIL. Develops backward stroke extension for swimmers who begin recovery too early.
how: While swimming, touch or brush the upper thigh with the thumb as far backward as possible without twisting the body sideways.

purpose_text: DETAIL, STRENGTH. Develops breath control.
how: For every x meters, breathe after every x pulls; for example, breathe every 3-5-7-9-11 pulls during each 25 or 50.

warnings.reason: Breathing every 3-5-7-9-11 strokes can become hypoxic training. The pattern, distance, and repetition should be individualized and stopped if dizziness or distress occurs.
The relationship between 'every x meters' and 'every x number of pulls' is not defined. The intended progression and unit of counting should be clarified before use.

purpose_text: ESSENTIAL, DETAIL. Encourages early vertical forearm (EVF).
how: Hold swim paddles with the fingers curled over the top so that each paddle sits closer to the forearm than in normal use. Swim freestyle slowly and observe how the paddle encourages a higher elbow at the start of the pull.

warnings.reason: Holding a paddle with the fingers curled over the top and the paddle shifted toward the forearm may strain the fingers and wrist or cause the paddle to release unexpectedly. Equipment fit and resistance should be limited.

purpose_text: ESSENTIAL. Develops timing, rotation, and overall stroke coordination.
how: Perform catch-up with the recovering arm pausing at mid-recovery, at approximately the shoulder line, and then switch arms. Use a full rotation with several extra kicks between strokes, or use no extra kicks and briefly balance on the side with the other arm extended forward. The goal is to complete the rotation. The recovery may use a bent or straight elbow, or an intermediate position, according to the freestyle style being practiced. The pull pattern may also vary accordingly.

warnings.reason: The stopping point in a three-quarter catch-up drill and the recovery-arm position vary by sprint and distance style in the description. The specific technical objective should be defined before instruction.

purpose_text: DETAIL. Develops the catch and the concept of anchoring the arm while the body moves past it, using body rotation and the recovering-arm action to move forward.
how: Use a paddle on 1 hand only. Set that arm in an early catch position in front, with the palm down, the elbow slightly flexed toward the ceiling, and the body rotated to the side. Keep the other arm at the side. Maintain the position of the paddled arm while using the recovery of the other arm and body rotation to move the body past it. Do not actively push backward with the paddled arm. The paddled arm should finish near the hip as the body moves past it. Repeat and switch the paddle every 50 or 100.

warnings.reason: Describing the paddle arm as an anchor that remains fixed while the body passes may oversimplify propulsion mechanics. The intended pressure, hand path, and body movement should be reviewed.

purpose_text: DETAIL. Develops stroke length and an immediate catch after entry rather than entering close to the head, sliding the hand forward underwater, dropping the elbow, and leading the pull with the elbow.
how: Swim freestyle very slowly, or perform a 6-kick 1-pull drill, with fully straight arms during recovery. Keep the elbows extended, circle the arms forward, and move directly into the catch. Keep the armpit out of the water until just before entry to provide feedback on rotation.

warnings.reason: A fully locked, straight-arm recovery may overload the shoulder in swimmers with limited mobility. Use a comfortable elbow position and stop if pain occurs.

purpose_text: APPRECIATION. Develops awareness of how elbow flexion during the pull changes the torque applied at the shoulder.
how: Use fins and a snorkel with a regular flutter kick. Keep 1 arm at the side and the other arm at the 6 o’clock position with the fingers pointing downward. Stabilize the shoulder so that the arm remains vertical. Kick first with the arm straight down, then with the elbow bent at 45 degrees, and then at 90 degrees with the elbow 1 inch below the surface and the forearm hanging downward. Compare the shoulder effort in each position as water resistance acts on the arm. The source explanation states that, at race speed, the hand remains relatively stable in relation to the pool bottom while much of the resistance is experienced by the moving upper arm and shoulder area. Observe the biceps and shoulder region while comparing the drag and torque.

warnings.reason: Holding the arm vertically to feel drag and shoulder torque may increase rotator-cuff loading. Use low speed, short duration, and an appropriate range of motion.
The specified hand position relative to the pool bottom and the claim that the upper arm and shoulder are the main sources of drag require biomechanical verification and clearer context.

purpose_text: BEGINNER. Stabilizes the core, develops spatial awareness in the water, maintains streamline, and uses the core to initiate rotation.
how: Begin with the arms at the sides and have the swimmer rotate slowly throughout the 25, either from side to side or through a full rotation. Use a flutter kick, with fins if needed. Then progress to a streamline position with the arms extended forward. Initiate rotation from the hips. Maintaining a slow, consistent rotation speed while keeping the body straight is difficult. Alternate the direction of rotation every length or after each full turn, and avoid excessive repetition because some young swimmers may become dizzy.

warnings.reason: Continuous whole-body rotation may cause dizziness, loss of orientation, or lane collision. Limit the number of rotations, alternate directions, and use a clear lane.

purpose_text: BEGINNER. Helps young swimmers learn the first steps of breaststroke and backstroke kicking.
how: Hold the board against the abdomen, lean the head back into the water, and perform either flutter kick or breaststroke kick. This is particularly useful for practicing breaststroke kick and recovering the knees together without also having to maintain flotation. During breaststroke kick, the knees may approach or emerge from the surface as described; during backstroke kick, the knees should remain underwater. Swimmers may briefly raise the head to observe the knees and feet.

warnings.reason: Allowing the knees to emerge during breaststroke kick while holding a board against the torso may alter the actual kick recovery pattern. The intended transfer to normal swimming should be reviewed.

purpose_text: BEGINNER. Encourages kicking from the hips and reduces excessive knee flexion.
how: Perform a backstroke kick. Raise the head into a supported reading position and observe the feet while kicking. The feet should create surface turbulence while the knees remain below the surface. Gradually lower the head back into the water without changing the kick.

warnings.reason: Repeatedly lifting the head to watch the feet may cause cervical fatigue and leg sinking. Use only briefly and return to neutral head alignment.

purpose_text: BEGINNER. Helps control the knees emerging from the water, such as bicycling during backstroke kick, or moving too wide during breaststroke kick.
how: Perform backstroke kick while holding a kickboard above the knees. The knees should not contact the board. The drill may also be performed with breaststroke kick to emphasize a narrow recovery; in that variation, both knees contact the board.

warnings.reason: Requiring both knees to contact a board during breaststroke kick may restrict knee width excessively. Board placement and the swimmer's natural hip structure should be considered.

name_en: KICK WITH PULL BUOY or RUBBER BANDS
purpose_text: BEGINNER. Encourages hip-driven dolphin kick and keeps the knees together during breaststroke kick.
how: Perform dolphin kick or breaststroke kick with a pull buoy between the thighs or a rubber band above the knees.

warnings.reason: Restricting the thighs or knees with a pull buoy or band during dolphin or breaststroke kick may create abnormal loading at the knees and hips. Use minimal resistance and stop if discomfort occurs.

purpose_text: ESSENTIAL. Kickboards may restrict natural body movement and elevate the upper body, which can cause the legs to sink or the knees to flex excessively. Limit kickboard use when the training goal is a flat, streamlined body position, while recognizing that social kick sets may support engagement and team cohesion.
how: Practice kicking for all strokes in multiple body positions: face-up, face-down, and on either side, with both arms up or down or with 1 arm in each position. Without boards, keep the body flat and streamlined. Use a snorkel to avoid unnecessary head movement, or breathe in the direction used for the stroke: forward for dolphin and breaststroke kick and to the side for flutter kick on the stomach. Alternatively, allow 1 technically correct stroke for breathing. Maintain streamline regardless of arm position. Practice side kicking to develop the upward kick and observe kick amplitude from the deck. Control kick size, speed, and effort. Initiate the kick from the hips without excessive lateral body movement. Include short accelerations from walls or blocks and occasional vertical kicking as appropriate.

warnings.reason: Combining explosive starts from blocks or walls with vertical kicking requires separate control of water depth, lane clearance, fatigue, and breathing demand.
The broad claim that kickboards restrict natural movement and cause the legs to sink may vary with body position, board size, and swimmer level. Treat the statement as context-dependent.

name_en: FLOATING OPEN TURN aka. FLOAT SNAP DRILL
purpose_text: Develops a quick change of direction during open turns and rapid movement of the knees toward the head.
how: Float, and then perform an open-turn movement into streamline in the opposite direction. The drill may be performed at the wall with the fingertips touching it or, for more advanced swimmers, in the middle of the lane. Use a pull buoy to improve flotation and keep the legs together.

purpose_text: Breathing is permitted during an open turn, but a lower head position may support a faster departure from the wall. Develop an adequate breathing reserve, particularly before a long breaststroke pullout.
how: Swim breaststroke to the wall, perform a somersault instead of an open turn, and push off into a full pullout.

warnings.reason: Encouraging an oxygen reserve for a long pullout may become breath-holding or hypoxic training. Limit distance and repetition and monitor each swimmer closely.
Performing a somersault instead of the required open turn after a breaststroke approach is not a competition-legal turn. The movement must be clearly labeled as training-only.

purpose_text: Slows the movement to allow focused practice of turn mechanics.
how: Perform the open turns toward the non-dominant side.

purpose_text: Helps improve push-off and breath control.
how: Instead of turning at the wall, submerge while using breaststroke, touch the pool bottom with both hands simultaneously, and turn upward toward the surface.

warnings.reason: Diving to the pool bottom, touching with both hands, and turning upward creates pressure, bottom-impact, orientation, and collision risks. Depth and lane access must be strictly controlled.

purpose_text: Develops awareness of whole-body resistance and a compact turn position. It also slows the turn to allow focused practice.
how: Perform a regular open turn, but submerge before the turn so that the wall contact occurs several feet below the surface while the entire body remains underwater.

warnings.reason: Touching the wall several feet below the surface with the entire body submerged limits visibility and increases head or shoulder impact risk. Use only in adequate depth with direct supervision.

purpose_text: Develops breath timing.
how: Kick with the hands on the wall and the head underwater. Exhale fully, and then perform an open turn with or without taking a breath.

warnings.reason: Exhaling completely before performing a turn may increase breath-holding, dizziness, or hyperventilation risk. Do not combine it with repeated maximal underwater efforts.

purpose_text: Helps athletes engage the core rather than relying on the hands to change momentum.
how: Perform a fast open-turn movement without touching the wall with the hands, while keeping the action as similar as possible to a normal turn.

warnings.reason: An open-turn action performed without touching the wall with the hands is not competition-legal for strokes requiring a simultaneous two-hand touch. Label it clearly as a training drill only.

purpose_text: Develops execution of the breaststroke pullout after a start or turn.
how:
Perform the sequence in the following order:
1. Jump from the blocks or push off the wall, enter streamline, and pause.
2. Perform a butterfly kick, and pause.
3. Perform the long pullout stroke, and pause.
4. Raise the shoulders toward the ears, and pause.
5. Recover the arms while performing the breaststroke kick, and bring the body to the surface with the hand action.

warnings.reason: The order and timing of the dolphin kick, arm pull, arm recovery, and breaststroke kick in the pullout should be checked against current competition rules and the coach's intended teaching sequence.

purpose_text: Repeats the pullout and practices returning the hands forward.
how: Perform several pullout pulls and arm recoveries in succession underwater after each wall without surfacing.

warnings.reason: Repeating several pullouts underwater increases breath-holding demand and hypoxic risk. Limit the number, distance, and recovery interval and provide direct supervision.
Multiple underwater pullouts are not permitted as a competition breaststroke start or turn sequence. The drill should be clearly identified as training-only.

purpose_text: Practices the approach to the wall.
how: Swim backstroke and finish the approach with the arm crossing over the head, reaching across while the shoulder remains raised.

warnings.reason: During a backstroke-to-breaststroke crossover approach, wall contact and body position must comply with current individual-medley transition rules. The exact legal version should be confirmed before race instruction.

purpose_text: Develops rapid movement of the knees toward the head.
how: Swim close to the lane line and grasp it. Bring the legs over on the opposite side, or directly overhead for a bucket turn. Move the knees toward the head and use the lane line as a leverage point to assist the leg rotation.

warnings.reason: Using the lane line as leverage while bringing the legs over creates finger-entrapment, lane-damage, and collision risks. Use only in an isolated lane with direct supervision.
Using the lane line as a support point is not a competition movement and must be clearly separated from legal transition-turn instruction.

purpose_text: Develops mechanics and integrates the backstroke-to-breaststroke transition turn.
how: Swim backstroke and perform a crossover or bucket turn in the middle of the pool. Practicing the movement in open water may support execution at the wall, where the contacting arm provides additional leverage.

warnings.reason: Crossover and bucket turns require legal wall contact and a legal backstroke finish position before the breaststroke transition. The drill should be checked against current individual-medley rules.
